title: Tabbed Folder Story Series Card Pack
audience: Families, homeschool groups, tutors, and adult-led writing tables for writers ages 6-11.
sessionLength: 16 printable tabbed folder story-series cards plus adult guide tools, series routines, take-home series slips, and optional adult prompts
safetyNote: No scary harm, no bullying, no romance, no weapons, no branded characters, no real child profiles.

cover.headline: Tabbed Folder Story Series Card Pack
cover.subhead: Sixteen tabbed folder cards help writers keep one fictional story series steady across private paper pages by returning to characters, settings, clue labels, and page-turn notes.

adultGuide.title: Tabbed Folder Story Series Adult Guide
bullets: Setup: choose one story folder, add three to five paper tabs, and label each tab with a simple story series part: ____________________.
Materials: keep blank pages, pencils, tab cards, paper clips, and a folder note sheet nearby before the adult-led session begins: ____________________.
Steps: help the writer place the current page behind the right tab, reread the last page softly, then plan the next page on paper: ____________________.
Safety: keep every name, place, and problem inside a made-up story world, and do not place child work online or ask for private details: ____________________.
Continuity: use the tab cards to track who is in the story series, what changed, and what the next page should remember: ____________________.
Reset: when the session ends, tuck loose pages into the story folder, mark the next tab to use, and write one adult reminder for later: ____________________.

seriesRoutines.title: Tab Check-In
adultSteps: The adult opens the story folder and asks which tab holds the current page: ____________________.
The child points to the tab and names the made-up story series part: ____________________.

seriesRoutines.title: Last Page Echo

seriesRoutines.familyLine: The next page will echo this detail from the last page: ____________________.

seriesRoutines.title: Series Thread Card

seriesRoutines.title: Next Page Bridge
adultSteps: The adult asks what the current page leaves unfinished in the pretend story: ____________________.

seriesRoutines.title: Folder Order Walk

cards.title: Buttonwood Library Train Story Series Card
cards.seriesSkill: connect a gentle paper story series by using a tabbed story folder to track one library-train rider, one returning car, and one carried clue
cards.useCase: Adult-led offline paper-only tabbed folder card for a Buttonwood Library Train story series: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: keep the work private and offline, label a story folder tab, and place page one beside a pencil: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Writer: with the adult, begin the library train page, then use the tab to keep the next page connected: ____________________.
cards.pageOneAnchorPrompt: Adult asks: On page one, name the Buttonwood Library Train, one rider, and the folder tab that will hold the story series: ____________________.
cards.characterReturnPrompt: Adult asks: Choose one rider, conductor, or shelf helper who returns on the next page and write their small job: ____________________.
cards.settingReturnPrompt: Adult asks: Pick one train place, such as the buttonwood bench car or the quiet card table, that returns in the story folder: ____________________.
cards.clueCarryPrompt: Adult asks: Carry one clue from page to next page, such as a brass button ticket, bookmark slip, or tiny track mark: ____________________.
cards.pageTurnPrompt: Adult asks: Write a next page line that tells where the train will stop when this tab opens again: ____________________.
cards.seriesWrapPrompt: Adult asks: At the end of the story series, point to the pages where the rider, train place, and clue stayed together: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: draw the tab label, then write one rider sentence and one next page stop: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Folder line: keep the Buttonwood Library Train pages under one tab and add a new paper stop later: ____________________.

cards.title: Cloudberry Clocktower Story Series Card
cards.seriesSkill: manage story series continuity by using a tabbed story folder to repeat a central character, clocktower setting detail, carried clue, and next-page question
cards.useCase: Adult-led offline paper-only tabbed folder card for a Cloudberry Clocktower story series: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: keep the work private and offline, label a story folder tab, and choose the first clocktower page to start: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Writer: with the adult, make each page connect to the page before it so the story series feels continuous on paper: ____________________.
cards.pageOneAnchorPrompt: Adult asks: On page one, set the Cloudberry Clocktower scene, name the main character, and write the tab title: ____________________.
cards.characterReturnPrompt: Adult asks: Decide what the main character notices each time they return, then add that reminder to the next page: ____________________.
cards.settingReturnPrompt: Adult asks: Choose one clocktower detail, such as the cloud bell, stair window, or minute hand mark, to repeat across pages: ____________________.
cards.clueCarryPrompt: Adult asks: Carry one clue forward, such as a paper gear sketch or cloud-shaped note, and write how it changes on the next page: ____________________.
cards.pageTurnPrompt: Adult asks: End the page with a next page question that belongs under this tab and points toward the carried clue: ____________________.
cards.seriesWrapPrompt: Adult asks: Reread the story folder pages and underline where the character, clocktower detail, and clue made one story series: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: write one page one anchor and one next page question under the same tab: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Folder line: add another Cloudberry Clocktower page that brings back the same character and clue: ____________________.

cards.useCase: Adult-led offline paper-only tabbed folder card for a Moon Muffin Market story series with no screens: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: keep the work private and offline, place this card under a story folder tab, and give the child one blank page: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Writer: with the adult, write page one about the moonlit market, then save the next page idea under the same tab: ____________________.
cards.pageOneAnchorPrompt: Adult asks: On page one, name the Moon Muffin Market, one helper, and the story folder tab that keeps the pages together: ____________________.
cards.characterReturnPrompt: Adult asks: Choose one market helper who comes back on the next page and write one kind job they do with paper signs: ____________________.
cards.settingReturnPrompt: Adult asks: Pick one moonlit stall detail, such as a silver bell, folded awning, or star tag, to return on the next page: ____________________.
cards.clueCarryPrompt: Adult asks: Carry one pretend clue from page to next page, such as a crescent token, paper label, or tiny lantern mark: ____________________.
cards.pageTurnPrompt: Adult asks: Write a next page line that tells what the helper will check when this tab opens again: ____________________.
cards.seriesWrapPrompt: Adult asks: Reread the story series pages and tap where the helper, market place, and paper clue show up again: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: write one helper sentence and one next page clue for the story folder: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Folder line: keep the Moon Muffin Market pages under one tab and add another gentle paper clue later: ____________________.
